content.body:
Originally a tank gun mount selected for economy and expediency, the QF.2pdr quickly became one of the wars best medium AT guns. Interwar British doctrine was that machineguns were for use against infantry, and direct-ire cannons were meant to deal with tanks, so the perfect weapon would be a medium caliber gun firing high-velocity solid shot. The 2lb.er was perfect.
Incorporating a number of good ideas, the carriage upon which it was mounted was ideal for high-speed travel, had 360-degree traverse as well as a full gunshield. In the early years of the war, it was capable of defeating most of the armor it faced. By the middle/end of the war it was obsolescent due to the ever-increasing armor on enemy tanks.
The QF.2pdr is an outstanding gun in Battleground Europe. It has an exceptionally flat trajectory making hits easy to score well out past 500m, the lack of high-magnification sights and range adjustment are its only shortcomings. The gunshield is good and the green color blends nicely into the terrain at any distance. The 360-degree traverse is especially welcome against the later war tanks that must be engaged from the sides or rear to have any chance of penetrating.
Engage all but the heaviest German tanks at 500m or so, but beware that they probably have better sighting optics than you do so if you allow them the opportunity to return fire, it will be deadly. Place yourself particularly in brush-lines where your distinctive silhouette will not be obvious.
